problem: Existing VLN frameworks assume static environments, panoramic action spaces and optimal expert supervision, so they overestimate Sim2Real ability and ignore dynamic humans sharing the space.
motivation: Real homes and offices contain moving people, so agents must perceive them and keep safe distances. The paper argues that relaxing these three assumptions (egocentric 60° FOV, dynamic humans, sub-optimal expert) exposes a large performance gap in current SOTA agents.
key_idea: Define Human-Aware VLN (HA-VLN) and build the HA3D simulator (SMPL humans in Matterport3D) plus the HA-R2R dataset, then provide CM/DT agents and human-aware metrics as a benchmark.
insight: Adding dynamic humans, an egocentric action space and sub-optimal supervision each sharply hurts existing agents: SR drops 46.7%/19.4% (seen/unseen) from static to dynamic, and 70.0%/43.8% from panoramic to egocentric. Retrained and zero-shot SOTA agents remain far below the Oracle (SR 0.89-0.91). A Decision Transformer trained only on random walks matches expert-supervised VLN-CM, while VLN-CM degrades badly when random data is mixed in. Adding a human-collision penalty to the reward does not help much, so better human-aware rewards are needed.
method: HA3D simulator: Matterport3D plus SMPL human motion (HAPS dataset: 145 activity descriptions, 435 MDM-generated motions, 120 frames each) rendered with Pyrender at 16 FPS; provides RGB-D at 60° FOV, navigable viewpoints and a human-collision signal (<1 m)
HA-R2R dataset: R2R paths annotated with human activities; GPT-4 rewrites instructions to include activities and relative positions, giving 21,567 instructions (avg 69 words, vocabulary ~4,500)
Oracle agent: A* on a navigation graph with human-affected nodes removed, with dynamic adjustment and rerouting; used as the sub-optimal expert and upper bound
VLN-CM: LSTM seq2seq with BERT instruction encoder, ResNet-152 visual features, cross-attention fusion and LSTM action decoder, trained with cross-entropy on Oracle demonstrations

VLN-DT: Decision Transformer with a cross-modal fusion module that weights language and vision, trained on 10^4 random-walk trajectories using target, distance and human-collision rewards with return-to-go
Human-aware metrics: TCR and CR (collisions within 1 m) plus collision-aware SR and NE, with critical-node adjustment

setting.backbone: VLN-CM: BERT + ResNet-152 + LSTM (trained); VLN-DT: BERT + ResNet-152 + causal transformer (trained); baselines Speaker-Follower, Rec-VLNBERT, Airbert
setting.training_data: HA-R2R with Oracle demonstrations (VLN-CM); 10^4 random-walk trajectories of max 30 steps (VLN-DT)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with 60° FOV (monocular RGB for the real robot)
setting.action_space: low-level egocentric: forward, left, right, up, down, stop (real robot: 0.5 m forward, 45° turn)
setting.simulator: HA3D (Matterport3D-based) with SMPL humans; real Unitree GO1 quadruped
setting.privileged: none at test time (the Oracle uses GT graph and human positions only for supervision/benchmark)

results: On HA-VLN, retrained SOTA agents reach at most SR 0.40 in unseen environments versus the Oracle's 0.89, and zero-shot agents drop up to about 72%. VLN-DT trained on random walks (SR 0.21 seen / 0.11 unseen) is comparable to expert-supervised VLN-CM (0.19 / 0.12). VLN-CM's SR falls to 0.03 / 0.02 when trained on 100% random data.
limitations: Both proposed agents perform poorly in absolute terms (SR ≤0.21) and are far below the Oracle
Human behavior is limited to basic motion (no social nuance or groups), and the environments are indoor only
Real-robot validation is qualitative (a few office demos, some collisions) with no quantitative results
